points.description: States the k-nearest-neighbours procedure: a new data point is classified by finding its k nearest neighbours among the already classified/coloured old data, taking a majority vote of their classes/colours, and assigning the new point to the class/colour with the most votes. Equivalent wording counts; the supervised/unsupervised label is not required.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions finding k nearest neighbours or majority voting/assignment but not both parts of the procedure.

levels.says: Mentions k nearest neighbours but not the majority-vote assignment, or mentions majority voting/assignment but not finding the k nearest neighbours.

points.description: Provides pseudo code (any reasonable syntax) that takes a new point, selects/finds its k nearest neighbours among the labelled/classified data, performs a majority vote of their labels, and returns or assigns the majority label to the new point. High-level pseudo code is acceptable; an explicit distance formula is not required.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if pseudo code is present but omits either selecting the k nearest neighbours or the majority-vote assignment, or is too vague to follow.

levels.says: Pseudo code is present but omits either selecting the k nearest neighbours or the majority-vote assignment, or is too vague to follow.

rubric.notes: Award P1 for the KNN procedure in words or pseudo code: find k nearest classified neighbours, take a majority vote, and assign the winning class. Award P2 only for pseudo code that implements that procedure; high-level pseudo code is acceptable. A correct idea without pseudo code earns P1 only, and pseudo code missing a key step earns half of P2.
